title: Repeatability and retry-solver mechanism of the G21F admissibility islands
question: Is the six-island status-0/status-6 topology observed by G21F deterministic across fresh immutable-origin participant sessions, and can its status-6 islands be localized to the preregistered transaction retry sequence ending in a physical solver rejection rather than mass or temporal-certificate unavailability?

source_reconciliation.transaction_semantics: A solver-failed attempt increments solver_rejections and enters reject_and_retry; at retry_index >= max_retries the transaction terminates TX_STATUS_RETRY_EXHAUSTED, which the canonical interval reports as CANONICAL_STATUS_TRANSACTION_FAILED.
source_reconciliation.limitation: Aggregate G15/G16 diagnostics establish counts but do not expose the final physical solver status/temporal observation. G21G may add a research-only bridge accessor for the already-public backend observation() snapshot. It may not change runtime execution or participant semantics.

frozen_scan.generation: numpy.linspace(lower_head_m, upper_head_m, 33, dtype=float64), requiring 33 unique binary64 heads

experiment_contract: Run the exact 33 frozen binary64 heads in three independent fresh G16 sessions from the same immutable FMR origin.
Every head in every session must cause one fresh physical participant trial; no cross-session or within-session cache reuse is allowed because heads are unique and sessions are reset.
For each head record the complete G15/G16 participant observation and, immediately after the physical trial, a research-only snapshot of corrector_backend%observation().

The backend snapshot accessor is read-only test infrastructure and may expose only existing observation values: solver execution/status/diagnostics and temporal-indicator/certificate diagnostics. It must not call a solver, mutate backend state, alter candidate liveness or publish authority.
Compare the complete 33-element participant-status vector across all three sessions and against the closed G21F vector.
Partition each vector into contiguous status islands and require identical island boundaries across sessions before any deterministic-mechanism classification.

For status-6 heads test the aggregate retry signature against attempts=9, retries=8, temporal_rejections=8, solver_rejections=1, accepted_substeps=0, mass_rejections=0 and temporal_unavailable_rejections=0. Report deviations rather than weakening this signature.

For status-0 heads report the distribution of accepted_substeps, attempts, temporal_rejections and final backend solver/temporal observation; do not preregister one required successful execution count beyond status=0/completed/candidate-ready.
Use source-contract assertions to bind result_status=2, max_retries=8, retry_scale=0.5 and the solver-rejection retry branch to current source.
End every session with unchanged accepted revision/time/ledger, no live participant candidate and false FMR/ledger preflight.

classification_rules.DETERMINISTIC_RETRY_SOLVER_BIFURCATION: All three status vectors and island boundaries exactly match G21F, and every status-6 head has the frozen aggregate retry-exhaustion signature with a non-converged final physical solver observation, while status-0 heads complete without solver rejection.
classification_rules.DETERMINISTIC_ISLANDS_MIXED_EXECUTION_CA: All three island topologies exactly reproduce, but status-6 heads do not share one retry/solver signature or backend observations show multiple terminal mechanisms.
classification_rules.NONDETERMINISTIC_ISLAND_TOPOLOGY: At least one fresh session changes any of the 33 participant statuses or contiguous island boundaries.
classification_rules.SOURCE_OR_INSTRUMENTATION_UNRESOLVED: Source bindings or read-only backend observation cannot be established without changing production/runtime semantics.

quantitative_gates: Three independent fresh sessions each execute exactly 33 physical participant trials for 33 unique heads and zero cache hits.
All three 33-element status vectors are reported and compared bit-for-bit to the G21F status vector.
All island start/end indices are reported per session.
All status-6 aggregate retry signatures and final backend solver statuses are reported.
No accepted state, ledger, candidate liveness or preflight authority leaks.
No production/runtime/adapter source changes. Only test bridge/wrapper, research test/workflow and evidence may change.
pass_interpretation: PASS qualifies only the repeatability/mechanism classification. It does not justify smoothing status islands, changing max_retries or temporal tolerances, choosing STANDARD/NOUR, or production-admitting response-space globalization.
fail_interpretation: Preserve failures. Do not alter the frozen 33 heads, retry policy, solver configuration, participant acceptance or status semantics after observing the result.
